title: Senate begins plenary deliberations for 2027 national budget
summary: Senators are proposing P204.634 billion in amendments in the 2027 national budget

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Senate on Monday, November 23, began plenary deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, with lawmakers proposing P204.634 billion in amendments that prioritize “basic needs,” including health care and education, while cutting billions of pesos in infrastructure projects.

Senator JV Ejercito, chairperson of the Senate finance committee, sponsored Committee Report No. 131 on House Bill No. 10858, or the General Appropriations Bill (GAB), formally bringing the proposed budget to the plenary for deliberations.
In his sponsorship speech, Ejercito bat for a “back to basics” approach in the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget, emphasizing the need to prioritize essential services.

“Health care, food security, education, livelihood, employment, and security — these are the things that we want to focus on during our outlining and deliberations of the 2027 national budget. Back to basics,” Ejercito said.
“Before we focus on complicated matters, we should focus what limited resources we have on ensuring that the basic needs of our people are provided,” he said.
The Senate’s P204.634-billion proposed amendments include a P97-billion reduction in the allocation for 3,463 projects of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

These include 36 DPWH buildings, 295 projects deemed noncompliant for lacking proper documentation under the National Expenditure Program, and 3,132 noncompliant projects that appeared only in the House-approved GAB.
Ejercito previously said the reductions in the DPWH budget would be realigned to foreign-assisted infrastructure projects, which saw a P130-billion decrease in the House-approved GAB.

Budget watchdogs People’s Budget Coalition and BetterGovPH had earlier flagged nearly 7,000 projects worth P190 billion that lacked published project attachments in the House-approved 2027 budget. PBC also tracked some 6,200 DPWH projects worth P170 million that were inserted into the budget.
“This, Mr. President, is the direction we want to pursue in the 2027 national budget. Back to basics, but with a clear vision for economic recovery and nation-building,” said Ejercito.
Under the Senate version of the budget, the health sector received a P52-billion increase, with funding partly sourced from realignments within the Department of Health (DOH).

State health insurer Philippine Health Insurance Corporation, or PhilHealth, received an additional P19.8 billion, raising its allocation from P74.4 billion under the House-approved GAB to P94.2 billion in the Senate version.

The DOH Office of the Secretary received an additional P9.6 billion, increasing its budget to P378.6 billion. This includes P5.49 billion for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program, P1.09 billion for health promotion programs, P1.5 billion for immunization programs, and P736 million for the Sulu transition.
The Senate realigned funding for medical assistance to the Zero Balance Billing program, allocating P1 billion for local government-run hospitals.

The education sector, meanwhile, received P915.4 billion in the Senate’s budget bill. Of this amount, P11.8 billion will go to the Department of Education, including P11 billion for the School-Based Feeding Program to support the universal feeding program for kindergarten to Grade 1 students.

State universities and colleges will receive P138.2 billion for the continued construction and improvement of their school buildings, with each SUC receiving P7.5 million for the Smart Campus Project — a program that would provide internet connectivity to over 100 campuses.
The Senate budget bill also provides additional P33.1 billion in funding for foreign-assisted infrastructure projects, primarily to restore funding cuts in the House-approved GAB.
Among these are P4.7 billion to restore the government’s counterpart funding for the Metro Manila Subway Project and P15 billion in loan proceeds for the North-South Commuter Railway project.
A combined P146.5 million will also be allocated for the NCR Busway Project, Active Transport Bike Share System, and Safe Pathways Program.
The Senate also allocated budget to enhance food security and ensure productivity of farmlands amid the threat of Super El Niño, earmarking P251 billion for the Department of Agriculture (DA).

This includes an additional P4 billion for the DA’s Rice Program to help boost rice production; a P250 million fund for programs helping farmers amid the impending drought; and an augmentation of P1 billion for the DA’s Quick Response Fund to “assist our farmers the earliest time the streams and wells show signs of drying up.”

More than P1 billion was allotted for the establishment of the storage facility Benguet AgriPinoy Trading Center, while P50 million and P200 million were allocated for the construction of a cold storage facility in Barlig, Mountain Province and Oriental Mindoro, respectively.
The Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development will also receive P4.04 billion to support the Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino Program.

Meanwhile, senators provided an additional P1.73 billion to the Department of National Defense, hiking its budget to P326.9 billion. This is on top of the P50 billion earmarked for the continued modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

Ejercito also underscored the need to strengthen the capabilities of the Philippine Navy to improve maritime patrols and reinforce the country’s presence in the West Philippine Sea. The Philippine Coast Guard, for its part, will receive P45.6 billion, including an additional P146.8-million allocation, to support its operations and maritime security efforts.

Ejercito filed the committee report on November 20. It was signed by 18 senators, including senators Tito Sotto, Migz Zubiri, Bam Aquino, Bong Go, Risa Hontiveros, Kiko Pangilinan, Erwin Tulfo, Joel Villanueva, Ping Lacson, Chiz Escudero, Lito Lapid, Raffy Tulfo, Imee Marcos, Robinhood Padilla, Mark Villar, Pia Cayetano, and Camille Villar.
In a manifestation, Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano explained why he did not sign the committee report.

“My signature is not on that committee report not because I did not want to sign but because it is physically impossible to come up with a good judgment, even if I do trust the chairman of the committee on finance, Senator JV,” Cayetano said.
Senators are working on a tight schedule to ratify the budget bill and avoid a reenacted budget in 2027.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said over the weekend that the country could not afford another reenacted budget, arguing that a fresh spending plan would help stimulate the economy.

“If we have a new budget, we will have new spending, because if we analyze it, one of our country’s economic problems is slow spending. So, the 2027 budget will serve as a stimulus program to it,” Gatchalian told DZBB Super Radyo.
The Senate is eyeing holding an open bicameral conference committee on the proposed 2027 budget on December 13, with ratification targeted for December 17.

Apart from the budget, the Commission on Appointments (CA) is also racing against time to process the appointments of at least 35 presidential appointees, including Cabinet secretaries, ambassadors, and military officers, before its December 17 adjournment.
Gatchalian said the CA would hold three hearings before the break, from 8 am to 12 pm, ahead of the Senate’s plenary budget deliberations at 1 pm.
Senators are hoping to conclude the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before the end of the year. The trial is currently on a brief break and is scheduled to resume on December 1.
“Whatever the ruling is — be it conviction or acquittal — the consensus is we want to finish the trial before end of the year,” Gatchalian added. – Rappler.com
